title: claim_many() omits the AVM owner-resolution that claim() performs, so AVM-managed-lock rewards are sent to the wrong recipient
claimed_impact: RewardsDistributor.claim() resolves the true beneficiary of an AVM-managed lock before transferring rewards: when avm is set and the tokenId is AVM-managed it sets _nftOwner = avm.getOriginalOwner(tokenId). Its sibling claim_many() runs the same _claim / ownerOf / transfer flow in a loop but omits the avm.getOriginalOwner branch entirely, so for AVM-managed locks it transfers the rewards to the raw ownerOf(tokenId) (the AVM contract) instead of the original owner. The original owner permanently loses the rewards. This is a sibling-function parity gap: the batch variant drops a recipient-resolution component the singular variant enforces on a shared transfer path. Confirmed HIGH-confidence recovery by the sibling_function_parity research detector (recipient_parity, missing component avm.getOriginalOwner); 0 high/medium false positives across the 16-subject eval corpus.
